packs.title: Timber, Trails & Motion
packs.promise: Read a working landscape, follow a woodland giant and meet mountain water on four separate outings.

q.s: Turn a comfortable indoor walk into an observation game.
st: Enter with valid admission and follow staff directions to an open walking area suitable for you.
At a comfortable pace notice one close detail, one across the room and one that changes as you move. Pause safely rather than trying a speed or fitness target.
Collect the three observations in notes and name the detail you would have missed while standing still.

q.t: A River Without the Word Blue
q.s: Write a tiny river portrait using other senses.
st: Find an open dry public viewpoint of the river without entering the play area or approaching a slippery edge.
Notice movement, sound and a nearby texture. Write a five-word river portrait without using the word blue.
Make a second five-word version from another safe viewpoint and choose which better fits what you noticed.

q.s: Collect three ways a mine visit explains its work.
st: Check in early for your booked tour and follow the guide’s equipment, route and conduct rules.
Collect three observations from what the guide actually shows or explains: a tool, a movement of material and a choice that helped people work underground. Do not invent a missing example.
After the tour, write a three-part shift report, separating your observation from what the guide explained. Photos are optional only with permission.

packs.title: Main Street in Small Chapters
packs.promise: Follow museum stories, public art and river details through two downtown afternoons.

q.t: A House at the Edge of the Path
q.s: Collect three exterior details from a historic-house park.
st: Use the open public park path outside buildings and planted areas.
Choose three visible exterior details from roof, opening, surface, trim or shadow actually present. Compare one with another rather than entering a building.
Record the three details and select one you would use to recognize the place on a return walk.

q.t: The Book You Did Not Expect
q.s: Write a six-word invitation from an unexpected subject.
st: Enter during public open hours and browse an available shelf outside your usual subject.
Choose a book you may read and find one idea or question that interests you; return it correctly.
Write an original six-word invitation to explore that subject. Use your own words and do not present them as the book’s quotation.

q.s: Compare how a current exhibition changes an old building.
st: Enter the offered exhibition within your valid ticket window and follow its actual visitor instructions.
Collect three observations about materials, color or scale in works actually available. Separate the historic room from the contemporary installation; do not assume touching is permitted.
Write which observed choice most changes the room’s atmosphere. No named artwork, specific artist or interactive effect is required.
